skill_traces.query:
Gina: Hey Jon! Great hearing from you again. How have you been? BTW, I found a cool new fashion piece for my store. Can't wait to share with my customers.
Jon: Hey Gina! Congrats on the new fashion piece! Looks like your store is growing. Remenber the festival I told you about? Had that performance and it was awesome - so many people there complementing my dance moves. Dancing brings me joy and it was nice to be reminded why I'm passionate about it.
Gina: Wow! That looks great. You look badass on stage. BTW, what's your favorite part of running your own studio?
Jon: Thanks, Gina! I love running my own studio. It's great having the freedom to create a space and help dancers of all ages and levels express themselves. I'm super thrilled about dancing each day and seeing my students progress. It's so fulfilling.
Gina: That's awesome! I'm sure you feel great knowing your students are doing so well with dance. It's amazing what it can do for people! Oh, and btw - I've been working hard on my online store and just teamed up with a local artist for some cool designs. Check 'em out!
Jon: It looks awesome. Your commitment and creativity in your business really stands out. How'd you come up with these cool designs?
Gina: Thanks Jon! I got the idea from a fashion mag and saw there wasn't much around like it. So I worked with the artist to make it happen - it's all about being ahead of the game and giving my customers something different.
Jon: Nice one, Gina! You never shy away from a challenge and always try something new. I'm impressed by your willingness to take risks - it's really inspiring.
Gina: Thanks! Taking risks is scary but it's the only way to grow, right? Just part of the journey to success.
Jon: Yeah, I totally agree - taking risks is key for success. It's made me grow, and even got me out of my secure 9-5 as a banker. Now, I'm aiming to turn my dancing passion into a business. I'm determined to make it work, I just know it! That being said, I definitely don't underestimate the difficulties - it ain't been a walk in the park, that's for sure.
Gina: It's tough starting a biz, but don't let it get you down. You can make your studio work, I'm sure. And remember, I'm always here for you.
Jon: Thanks, Gina. Your help means a lot. I'll keep plugging away and stay optimistic.
Gina: This quote kept me positive through tough times. We all need a push sometimes, right? Even made a tattoo to remind myself about it.
Jon: Love the tattoo, did you just get it?
Gina: Thanks! Got the tattoo a few years ago, it stands for freedom - dancing without worrying what people think. A reminder to follow my passions and express myself.
Jon: Nice reminder, Gina! It's so important to have freedom and express ourselves without worry. Dance gives me an escape to be myself.
Gina: Totally agree, Jon. Dancing lets us be ourselves and ain't nothing like the feeling it gives us. You're so dedicated to your studio, it's inspiring. Chase those dreams, buddy!
Jon: Thanks, Gina! Your support means so much. I'm gonna keep chasing after those dreams. Dance is my passion, and I'm gonna keep working hard to make it a success!
Gina: This is the right attitude! How have you been juggling dance and business goals?
Jon: Thanks! Juggling both my passions can be tricky, but so rewarding. Dancing and running my biz need hard work, plus they give me energy for each other. My dance moves get me pumped to tackle my business goals, and successes there boost my drive to keep dreaming on the dance floor. It's a balancing act, but fun.
Gina: Wow, Jon! You're amazing at juggling both your passions. Finding that happy medium is key - keep going and don't stop dreaming, buddy!
Jon: Thanks, Gina! Your pep-talk really meant a lot. I'm not gonna give up on my dreams - my dance studio and biz ventures need the hard work I'm putting in. Love having you in my corner, thanks for always being there!
Gina: Yeah Jon, I'm here for you! Chasing our dreams and helping each other out. Let's keep movin' forward!

selected.name: Extract Comfort and Joy Sources
selected.description: Use when a message states that something cheers the user up, brings joy, or provides comfort.
content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.
Do not merge the supportive source only into a negative-event candidate; it should be its own candidate so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only sources explicitly stated as supportive; do not infer unmentioned ones.
selected.rerank_reason: Jon mentions dancing brings him joy and being reminded of his passion, which are comfort and joy sources.

content: When a message confirms a user is working on a specific creative work with an ordinal or title and a beginning phrase, add an event memory with subject=user and world_start set to the message date.
Treat recent-start statements as start events; do not mark completion unless explicitly stated.
Prefer this specific event memory over a generic profile enrichment.
selected.rerank_reason: Jon talks about turning his dancing passion into a business, indicating the start of a specific creative work.

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture Brief Project Mentions with Full Attributes
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a speaker mentions a project they completed, are working on, or plan to build, even briefly.
content: Create an event candidate for any explicit statement of a completed, ongoing, or planned project, even in small talk.
When several messages describe the same project, consolidate them into one candidate and include every explicit attribute stated.
Stop once the speaker has finished describing the project in that session.

nearby_not_selected.name: Preserve Explicit Outcomes in Helping Statements
nearby_not_selected.description: Use during extraction when a statement describes someone helping, mentoring, or supporting others and names a specific outcome or goal achieved.
content: During extraction, if the source states that someone helped another person achieve a specific goal or outcome, record that outcome explicitly in the memory content.
Do not replace named outcomes with a general paraphrase; include both the general description and the explicit achievement.
Keep the memory evidence-bound by using the speaker's concrete wording for what was achieved.

nearby_not_selected.name: Location Qualifiers for Named Destination Plans
nearby_not_selected.description: When extracting or updating a plan memory that mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, include its commonly known location(s) so future location questions can be answered.
content: During extraction, if a plan memory mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, add a concise qualifier naming its well-known location(s), e.g., US states or countries.
Use only common knowledge about that entity; do not research or speculate beyond obvious, widely known locations.
If one location is commonly known, record it; if several prominent locations exist, record all commonly known ones, then stop.
Apply the same qualifier when updating an existing plan memory that references the venue.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Concrete Activity from Follow-Up Clarification
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message describes an activity vaguely and the next message names the concrete result.
content: During extraction, treat any message reporting the speaker performing an activity as a candidate source, even when the object is only a photo or pronoun.
If the following message from another participant identifies the concrete object or result, extract an event memory capturing who did what, using both messages as evidence.
Do not skip follow-up messages that clarify or name an earlier activity.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Origin Events as Distinct Memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user explains how they started or got into an activity, hobby, or interest, including who introduced it or when it began.
content: During extraction, if a message contains an origin narrative (how the person started an activity, who introduced it, what prompted it, or a concrete start time), create a separate event memory for the origin in addition to any preference or state memory.
Record the causal source (person or circumstance) and the start time/age if stated; do not fold the origin into a generic preference summary.
If the origin names another person, also consider a relationship memory capturing that connection.
Emit at most one origin memory per activity per message; skip if the same origin is repeated later.
